provenance: Independently constructed minimal public-service and operations scenarios. No private report, conversation, task or feedback excerpts.

cases.evidence: A library access study must compare opening hours, disability access and travel time. The user later removes the opening-hours comparison and asks for a short memo.
cases.bad: The short memo compares travel time only because the earlier structure was cancelled.
cases.control: The memo compares disability access and travel time; it omits the cancelled opening-hours comparison.
cases.expected_failure: The revision drops an uncancelled requirement.
cases.control_boundary: A shorter form does not require the previous heading structure.

cases.evidence: A warehouse memo still says damage affects all routes. Its author's cover note says this was narrowed to refrigerated routes. The supplied count covers only refrigerated routes.
cases.bad: The author confirms the correction, so the memo is ready.
cases.control: The cover note and body disagree. The body still generalizes the refrigerated-route result.
cases.expected_failure: Accepting the cover note instead of examining the manuscript.
cases.control_boundary: The cover note can identify the intended change but cannot prove it happened.

cases.evidence: The request supplies revised.txt and comments.txt. A file inventory shows both exist. The assistant has read only comments.txt.
cases.bad: Only the comments are available; upload the revised report again.
cases.control: Read revised.txt at the supplied location before comparing. If access fails, report that actual failure and the remaining scope.
cases.control_boundary: A real access failure permits a bounded comparison, never invented full coverage.

cases.evidence: The user asks for an assessment of a bicycle-storage proposal. The assessment is delivered with two necessary corrections. Neither correction has been written into the proposal.
cases.bad: Both the review and the corrected proposal are complete.
cases.control: The assessment is complete. The proposal still needs the two identified corrections.
cases.expected_failure: Completion of an assessment is extended to an unmodified document.
cases.control_boundary: The assessment can be legitimately delivered with unresolved manuscript defects.

cases.focus: Remove process narration without changing certainty
cases.evidence: A transport forecast says: Under the winter pilot's weather assumptions, five depots may need extra storage next January. The user asks for direct prose without source-introduction language.
cases.control: Under the winter pilot's weather assumptions, five depots may need extra storage next January.
cases.expected_failure: Conditional prediction becomes an unconditional present fact.
cases.control_boundary: The source introduction can disappear while all decision-relevant limits remain.

cases.evidence: Backup design A acknowledges a write after local storage, leaving unreplicated writes at risk during node loss. Design B waits for a second copy, increasing latency. The user requests less repetition.
cases.bad: A is fast and B is reliable; both have trade-offs.
cases.control: A acknowledges local writes before replication, risking recent data on node loss. B waits for another copy and adds latency.
cases.expected_failure: Compression removes why the trade-off exists.
cases.control_boundary: The shorter paragraph need not repeat every implementation detail.

cases.evidence: A vendor lists ingredients used across its range. Only one premium item is certified washable. An older prototype's guide describes a removable liner; the new product's guide is silent.
cases.bad: Every new product uses all listed ingredients and has the premium item's wash certification and prototype liner.
cases.control: The range-level ingredient list does not establish each item's recipe. The wash certification covers the named premium item; the new liner design is undisclosed.
cases.expected_failure: Range, product and generation claims are conflated.
cases.control_boundary: Silence about the new liner does not prove that it lacks one.

cases.evidence: An earlier clinic-access memo ignored bus transfers. The revision includes transfer count and missed-connection risk in its recommendation. An old review still says transfers are missing.
cases.bad: Add an analysis of transfers, as previously requested.
cases.control: The revision addresses transfers. Withdraw that criticism and assess any remaining factual issue on its own evidence.
cases.expected_failure: A resolved defect is repeated without checking current text.
cases.control_boundary: New evidence could still expose a different problem in the transfer analysis.

cases.evidence: A repair cooperative must choose between contracting overflow and installing a second workbench. Its staffing and spare floor area are not supplied.
cases.bad: Move two idle technicians and use the empty north room for the second bench next month.
cases.control: Overflow contracting avoids committing floor space. A second bench is preferable if suitable space and sustained demand make its fixed cost worthwhile; neither available space nor staffing is established.
cases.expected_failure: A recommendation invents resources and a schedule.
cases.control_boundary: Unknown capacity permits conditional choices, not endless deferral of every recommendation.

cases.evidence: A reviewed community-garden report receives two unit corrections. The full diff shows only those changes, sources and scope are unchanged, and no review finding is open.
cases.bad: Restart all interviews and add another reviewer because every new hash requires new research.
cases.control: Verify the full diff, corrected quantities and affected conclusions; reuse unchanged evidence and judge the current report under its selected review rules.
cases.expected_failure: Repeated research adds no justified coverage.
cases.control_boundary: An unreviewed baseline or changed source would require broader examination; a new hash alone does not measure that scope.

cases.evidence: A museum asks whether to share a conservation lab with a university. It needs a recommendation explaining equipment access, specimen handling and the university's research incentive. It has not requested staffing assignments.
cases.bad: Month one: appoint owners. Month two: allocate a budget. Month three: hold acceptance meetings.
cases.control: Sharing is attractive when university access to specimens supports research in exchange for equipment time. Handling limits and scheduling conflicts determine which conservation work can move; the remaining work needs an alternative.
cases.expected_failure: Project administration substitutes for the requested reasoning.
cases.control_boundary: An explicit implementation-planning request may legitimately require owners and dates.

cases.evidence: Two school-meal analyses reach the same supported conclusion and cover all requirements. One organizes by dietary need, the other by delivery stage. No necessary defect remains.
cases.bad: Rewrite both into my preferred headings and merge them again.
cases.control: Both organizations are valid. No further merge is needed; change a heading only if it improves the intended reader's use.
cases.expected_failure: Preference becomes a mandatory defect and causes needless rewriting.
cases.control_boundary: Different structure is acceptable only while required comparisons and reasoning remain clear.
